translation:
The target defines a record type `S3` parameterized by four arbitrary types `P`, `D`, `E`, and `R`, together with seven definitions (`D17` through `D23`) parameterized by a value `t : S3 P D E R` (none of which assert or prove any theorem; the `Prop` definitions only define predicates):

1. `S3 P D E R`: A structure with four fields and no axioms or constraints linking them:
   - `c1 : P → Set D` (assigns to each `p : P` a set of elements of `D`),
   - `c2 : D → Set E` (assigns to each `o : D` a set of elements of `E`),
   - `c3 : D → R` (maps each element of `D` to an element of `R`),
   - `c4 : R → E` (maps each element of `R` to an element of `E`).

2. `D17 t : Set D`: The set of all `o : D` for which there exists some `p : P` with `o ∈ t.c1 p` (i.e., the union of `t.c1 p` over all `p : P`).

3. `D18 t o : Prop` (for `o : D`): The proposition that `o ∈ t.D17` (so `o ∈ t.c1 p` for some `p : P`) and `t.c4 (t.c3 o) ∉ t.c2 o`.

4. `D19 t r : Set P` (for `r : R`): The set of all `p : P` for which there exists `o : D` such that `o ∈ t.c1 p` and `t.c3 o = r`.

5. `D20 t p : Set E` (for `p : P`): The set of all `e : E` for which there exists `o : D` such that `o ∈ t.c1 p` and `e ∈ t.c2 o` (i.e., the union of `t.c2 o` over all `o ∈ t.c1 p`).

6. `D21 t r : Prop` (for `r : R`): The proposition that there exist a function `S : t.D19 r → t.D19 r` (mapping elements of the set `t.D19 r` to elements of `t.D19 r`) and an element `p` of `t.D19 r` such that the intersection `t.D20 p.1 ∩ t.D20 (S p).1` is empty (where `p.1` and `(S p).1` are the underlying elements of `P`). Note that both `S` and `p` are existentially quantified (`∃ S, ∃ p`): `S` is not required to satisfy the disjointness condition for all elements of `t.D19 r`, nor is `S` required to have any other property (such as differing from the identity, so `(S p).1` may equal `p.1` if `t.D20 p.1 = ∅`). Because `S` can be chosen as a constant function, `D21 t r` is logically equivalent to the existence of two (not necessarily distinct) elements `p, q ∈ t.D19 r` with `t.D20 p ∩ t.D20 q = ∅`.

7. `D22 t r : Prop` (for `r : R`): The proposition that there exists `o ∈ t.D17` such that `t.c3 o = r` (equivalently, there exist `p : P` and `o ∈ t.c1 p` with `t.c3 o = r`, i.e., `t.D19 r` is nonempty).

8. `D23 t : Prop`: The proposition that for every `r : R`, if `t.D22 r` holds, then `t.D21 r` holds. (Neither `t.c4` nor `D18` appears in `D19` through `D23`.)

divergences.description: In the source ([P-K2] and Definition 2.1), inference is introduced as a function inf(o) on datasets o ∈ O, with o_r only informally described as 'the part of the dataset which is used for inferring the state of experience'. The Lean structure S3 bakes in the strengthening that inf depends solely on o_r by typing c4 : R → E and evaluating t.c4 (t.c3 o) in D18 (an explicitly declared idealization that matches the intended semantics).

Definition 3.2 in [P-K31] quantifies 'for every o_r' without explicitly stating the domain of o_r. Because R is an arbitrary ambient type in Lean, D23 disambiguates this via D22 to range only over r : R that arise as t.c3 o for some o ∈ O = t.D17 (explicitly declared; note also that if O is empty, D23 holds vacuously).

The fields c1 : P → Set D (obs) and c2 : D → Set E (pred) allow empty images. While [P-K2] does not explicitly require nonemptiness (calling pred(o) 'a subset' and obs a correspondence generalizing functions), allowing pred(o) = ∅ permits D21 to hold vacuously via the identity map S = id whenever pred ∘ obs(p) = ∅ for some p ∈ P_{o_r}.

judgement.summary: The Lean definitions faithfully render Kleiner and Hoel's correspondences obs and pred, the dataset class O, falsification (Definition 2.1), P_{o_r}, pred ∘ obs(p), o_r-substitution (Definition 3.1), and universal substitution (Definition 3.2). The only divergences are minor idealizations and disambiguations—chiefly the declared choices of factoring inf through the inference content R and restricting universal substitution to realized inference contents, plus allowing empty images for obs and pred.
